neighbours.label: 'open' in the electrical sense (open contact, open drain / collector, open circuit)
fire: Each output stage is an open collector transistor that needs a pull-up.
Use the normally open terminal so the lamp lights only when the relay energizes.
A broken wire behaves like an open circuit and no current flows.
The sensor has an open drain interrupt line shared with other chips.
When the switch is open, the voltage across it equals the supply.
Check whether the fuse has failed open with a continuity tester.
The I2C bus uses open drain outputs on both SDA and SCL.
With the contacts held open, the motor stays off.
quiet: Each output stage drives the LED through a small resistor.
Use the common terminal so the lamp shares the ground with the relay.
A broken wire means the lamp will not light at all.
The sensor has an interrupt line shared with other chips.
Please keep the lab door open while the soldering fumes clear.
Check whether the fuse is the right rating for the circuit.
The I2C bus uses two wires called SDA and SCL.
The workshop is open to students every Tuesday evening.

notes: The + pole is logic levels (default LOW, logic ONE); output of this pole promotes contact/switch. Two near misses use non-electrical 'open'.
